svg.text: Encoder / embedding models on Spyre: target state
Model used: multilingual-e5-large · Compile Mode: True
Per-step serving path
vLLM Scheduler, used as-is
batches S requests carrying T tokens in total · chunked prefill off · never subclassed, its output never mutated
Token-count bucket dispatch
override of _determine_batch_execution_and_padding → round T up to the next compiled bucket, giving T_padded
upstream this hook pads to a captured CUDA graph; here to a compiled shape · pad rows zeroed · also cuts torch-spyre per-op recompiles
Compiled model body: one graph per token bucket (fullgraph, dynamic=False)
sees only the flat token list [T_padded, hidden], with no request boundaries · all layers share op shapes, so cost scales with distinct T, not with depth
Embeddings → N × [ Q · K · V projections (un-fused) · output projection · FFN ×2 · LayerNorm ×2 ]
N = 24 for multilingual-e5-large · 6 matrix multiplies per layer, 5 of them outside attention
torch.ops.vllm.unified_attention_with_output · opaque boundary
Dynamo does not trace inside. Selected by the platform's opaque_attention_op() → True, which TorchSpyrePlatform inherits from CpuPlatform
Encoder attention: the only request-aware stage
dense-grid strategy (compared with the planned flash variant at the foot of this diagram) · rounds up its own grid: S to a power of two, L already 64-aligned
Batch-shape tables, built once per step and carried on the attention metadata
additive mask + three gather index lists · derived from S and the per-request lengths, so identical for every layer
gather_pack
[T, H, D] → [S, H, L, D]
pad slots point at a zero row
SDPA on device
bidirectional, additive mask
one fused kernel per (S, L)
gather_unpack
[S, H, L, D] → [T, H, D]
single bulk output copy
tables on the metadata instead of rebuilt per layer ⇒ roughly 4 host/device barriers per pass, not one set per layer
Pooler on device: CLS / LAST / MEAN
row gather via index_select · L2 normalize via rsqrt · reads only real rows, using the per-request offsets
eager today · spyre_pooler.py subclasses the upstream poolers; compiling it is its own work item, not a warmup
MEAN on device needs a compile-safe segment sum and torch-spyre#3507 (index_add). Until both land, MEAN pools on the host and the hidden state crosses each step.
Pooled vectors → host
only [num_reqs, hidden] crosses the boundary · padded rows are discarded, never pooled
Shape vocabulary
T · tokens in the step
sum of the batched prompt lengths · bucketed to 64 / 128 / 256 / 512 tokens
S · requests in the step
how many prompts are batched together · bucketed to 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 …
L · the width of attention's grid
every request gets one row of L columns; L = align_up(longest prompt, 64)
short requests leave their remaining columns as padding
Worked example, prompts of 40, 12 and 58 tokens:
T = 110 → T_padded = 128 · S = 3 → 4 · L = 64 · grid = 4 × 64. Note S × L ≠ T.
Compilation mode
CompilationMode.STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE
torch.compile(model, backend="inductor",
fullgraph=True, dynamic=False)
dynamic=False → sizes are baked in as constants. A graph built for
128 tokens works only for 128; a new count means a new compile.
Startup: warmup walks both ladders
for T in token buckets: _dummy_run(T)
one compiled body graph per bucket
for (S, L): _dummy_run(force_attention=True)
without the flag no attention metadata is built,
so the attention path is never traced or compiled
_dummy_pooler_run(hidden_states)
warms pooler shapes · upstream's version is only a memory probe
warms
Design invariants
· The attention metadata always describes the real batch, so no
padded row is ever gathered into a request or pooled.
· Padding the body is safe because each layer treats every token
row on its own.
Attention shape strategy: the dense grid used above, and how flash attention would change it
A · Dense grid, the strategy shown above
Pack the ragged flat list into a rectangle, so every shape is fixed at compile time.
Needed because an offset computed from data does not lower under compilation
(torch-spyre#3508) — and that arithmetic is exactly what flash relies on. Eager
tolerates it; compiled mode, our target, does not.
· build an additive mask [S, 1, L, L] marking padding and cross-request slots
· build three index lists, then gather Q / K / V into [S, H, L, D]
· one fused SDPA kernel per (S, L), then gather the results back out
Shape axes: T for the body, (S, L) for attention. Two ladders to warm.
Costs: the mask grows with L² · index lists and a barrier per gather.
Works today. This is the current implementation.
B · Flash-style attention, planned
Never materialise the rectangle. Each block of queries reads its request's offset from the
metadata at runtime and works directly on the flat list, carrying a running softmax maximum
and sum — the online-softmax structure the Spyre decoder path already uses over KV pages.
· no [S, 1, L, L] mask; request boundaries are the offsets
· no gather_pack / gather_unpack; the kernel reads the flat list directly
· no per-layer index lists, so no per-gather barriers
Shape axis: block count, bucketed like the decoder's page loop. L disappears.
Both upstream backends already work this way: flash attention consumes the flat list with
cu_seqlens_q = query_start_loc, and the CPU backend passes query[:num_actual_tokens]
straight to a C++ kernel. Neither pads into a rectangle.
If flash attention lands, the diagram above simplifies and converges on the upstream design:
· the second shape axis collapses; bucket T and a block count, which is much closer to upstream's single axis
· the "batch-shape tables" box disappears, and with it the per-layer rebuild problem and its host/device barriers
· gather_pack / SDPA / gather_unpack collapse into one blocked-attention kernel
· the mask's L² growth at long prompts disappears, today's largest untested risk at realistic prompt lengths
Open question: whether a Spyre kernel can do the runtime offset arithmetic this depends on. If it cannot, the block
count stays bucketed. Everything else holds either way: padding seam, unpadded metadata, warmup, compilation mode.
